grain: 100% malted barley; kettle-soured mash and sour-fermented whisky
identity: Two Brewers Innovative Release No. 22, bottled in 2020 at 51% ABV. Unique numbered release rather than the permanent Classic or Peated expression.
short_version: A distinct sour-fermented Yukon malt, with lively fruit, aromatic spice and a dry peppery edge; the small independent review sample limits scoring confidence.
producer: Yukon Brewing / Two Brewers, Whitehorse, Yukon
production: The producer documents a blend of kettle-soured and sour-fermented malt whisky. Exact 2020 Release 22 was bottled at 51% ABV; Whiskybase lists 820 bottles and a 750 mL sample. No specific label age has been independently verified.
finish: Fermentation-led production distinction; no separate finishing-cask statement verified.
history: Two Brewers whisky grew from Yukon Brewing in Whitehorse, with numbered releases grouped into styles.
Release 22 was produced as an Innovative series malt; sour fermentation is the identity distinction, not an assumed cask finish.

reviews.summary: Matched member tasting descriptions praise aromatic fruit, sweetness and peppery spice; the extra strength is seen as beneficial. A small number of ratings is not a broad consensus.

quality_rationale: Independent exact-release notes indicate clean, distinctive sour-fermentation complexity and a pleasant peppery finish, while the very small review pool caps confidence at a provisional very-good level.
quality_confidence: Low-medium; only a limited exact-bottle member review record.
evidence_limit: Exact 2020 numbered release; producer tasting notes excluded from independent score.

grain: 100% malted barley with peated-malt component; exact peat proportion undisclosed
identity: Two Brewers Special Finishes Release No. 33, 2022, 58% ABV, nine years old; approximately three years of PX sherry influence across two casks.
short_version: Powerful, fruity PX-finished nine-year Yukon malt whose peat stays surprisingly well integrated in the best independent account; limited review breadth remains a concern.
producer: Yukon Brewing / Two Brewers, Whitehorse, Yukon
production: Contemporaneous Canadian trade material reports 299 bottles, nine-year age, 58% strength and approximately three years in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Two casks were necessary when a stave failed in the first. A peated-malt component is documented, without an exact proportion.
finish: About three years of Pedro Ximénez sherry influence including transfer between casks after a failed stave.
history: The Two Brewers numbered programme varies in recipe and age; Release 33 is a Special Finishes release rather than a standard Classic bottle.
The unusual cask-transfer history is material to the exact Release 33, not a generic property of every PX release.

reviews.summary: Direct comparison describes especially good fruit-peat integration, rich sweetness and well-managed wood, with a strongly favorable personal assessment.

quality_rationale: The matched independent comparison strongly praises integration of sherry fruit, peat and strength. One substantive reviewer is insufficient to extrapolate a 9/10 category consensus, so the provisional score stays excellent-to-very-good.
quality_confidence: Low-medium; a substantive head-to-head but narrow tasting sample.
evidence_limit: Individual enthusiast enthusiasm is not counted as widespread consensus.

grain: 100% malted barley, selected from fourteen mashes
identity: Two Brewers Classic Release No. 35, 46% ABV, issued in 2022; Canadian and export packaging sizes vary.
short_version: An eight-plus-year Classic Yukon malt with fruit, caramel and persistent spice in positive reviews, but sharper grain and tartness in independent counterpoints.
producer: Yukon Brewing / Two Brewers, Whitehorse, Yukon
production: A detailed independent review describes fourteen malted-barley mashes aged eight years or longer, combined from ex-bourbon and virgin-oak maturation. Exact reviewed Release 35 appears as a 46% 2022 Canadian/export bottling.
finish: Ex-bourbon and virgin oak maturation; no separately authenticated finishing stage.
history: Two Brewers' numbered Classic series includes release-by-release differences in maturity and assembly.
Release 35 is distinguished from the heavily PX-influenced Release 33 and Innovative sour-fermented Release 22.

reviews.summary: Rich sweet toffee, fruit and cream with peppery spice, framed as well-integrated.
Some enjoyable fruit but greater wood sharpness and less flavor development than expected.
Finds citrus/tartness and some feinty grain character; a more reserved assessment.

quality_rationale: A positive independent tasting identifies creamy integration and spicy persistence; exact-release consumer and blog counterpoints find sharper and tart notes. The balanced category-relative result is very good but evidence-limited.
quality_confidence: Medium; several independent sources with substantial disagreement.
evidence_limit: Do not count producer prizes or notes as independently measured quality.

grain: Canadian blended grain whisky with rye character; proportions not independently published
identity: Windsor Canadian Original, standard 80-proof blended Canadian whisky, distinguished from the 93.2-proof Windsor Reserve.
short_version: A gentle, fruity, rye-spiced Canadian mixer with modest body and a short, pleasant finish, supported by a detailed historical rather than current-production tasting.
producer: Alberta Distillers / Suntory Global Spirits; current brand marketing by Prestige Beverage Group
production: The standard 40% Windsor Canadian is a lighter Canadian blend with documented rye influence but no authenticated exact mash percentages. Published historical tasting emphasizes mixed citrus, caramel and spice.
finish: No separately verified finishing regimen; oak-aged Canadian blend.
history: Introduced in the 1960s as Windsor Supreme, the brand passed through several corporate owners.
The principal independent tasting was based on a 2011 sample and later rescored; formulation stability through 2026 is not assumed.

reviews.summary: Detailed historical assessment of rye-forward fruit, sweet grain, butterscotch, maple, light spice and a relatively short finish; judged solid for affordable mixing.

quality_rationale: A dated but substantial independent review indicates a smooth and functional inexpensive Canadian whisky, with limited complexity and shorter finish. Quality is category-relative and flagged historical-sample provisional.
quality_confidence: Low-medium; one comprehensive historical review, no proof of unchanged 2026 formula.
evidence_limit: 2011 tasting does not guarantee the same recipe in contemporary stock.

identity: Alberta Premium 20 Year, 2019 limited 42% ABV release, not the 25/30-year editions or 2019 Cask Strength edition.
short_version: Unusually mature all-rye Canadian whisky with deep spice and supple oak in its best showings, complicated by conflicting evidence about solvent-like off-notes and low-proof texture.
producer: Alberta Distillers, Calgary / Suntory Global Spirits
production: The 2019 limited edition was produced from 100% Canadian rye matured for 20 years, bottled at 42% ABV. The launch circulated a CAD $89.95/750 mL price which is not a current USD value reference.
finish: Extended oak maturation; no verified discrete finishing stage.
history: The limited 20-year release was marketed in 2019 alongside the separate first Alberta Premium Cask Strength edition.
The 20-year expression is not the brand's historically older 25- or 30-year standard bottles.

reviews.summary: Finds developed oak, banana bread, citrus and surprisingly forceful rye spice for the bottling proof.
Reports silky caramel, spice and raisin sweetness with a layered and long woody finish; favorable 87/100.
Finds an intrusive industrial/solvent nose, thin texture and much shorter finish; strongly dissenting evidence.

quality_rationale: Positive independent accounts value mature rye complexity and oak integration, while a sharply negative exact-release tasting flags solvent-like and thin qualities. These conflicts support only provisional very-good quality.
quality_confidence: Medium; several exact-identity in-depth reviews conflict.
evidence_limit: Score deliberately reflects conflicting samples and does not infer universal satisfaction.

finish: Ten-year maturation; no separate finishing process independently established.
